text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpu-pool-exhausted - GPU autoscaler failed to scale the 'inference-prod' pool. Queue length 1200, p99 latency > 10s. Customers seeing throttling. Links: https://infra/redwood/incidents/1752506789

alex (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming impact, paging SRE channel.

maria (sre): I see the queue growth in the dashboard. Autoscaler logs show repeated backoff from cloud API: "RateLimitExceeded" and "QuotaExceeded". Trying to trigger manual scale.

alex (oncall): Do the manual scale now. If cloud quota is the issue, we need to move traffic to fallback pool.

tariq (runtime): Trying manual scale: 
```
# increase pool by 4 nodes
redwoodctl pool scale inference-prod --add-nodes 4
```
Result: "400 QuotaExceeded: GPU quota reached in region us-west1"

sam (eng): Can we divert low-priority traffic to the bursty-batch pool, and reserve capacity for paid customers?

alex (oncall): Yes. Maria, please apply throttling on anonymous/free routes and enable prioritized_queue for enterprise routes.

maria (sre): Applying runtime controls:
```
# throttle free tier to 10 rps
redwoodctl config set route /v1/generate --rate-limit 10 --selector free
# enable priority routing
redwoodctl config set routing priority=true --selector enterprise
```
Applied. Monitoring.

kelly (support): Notifying customers: Affected customers list: cust-omega, beta-platform, integrator-x. Messaging prepared: "We're experiencing capacity-related throttling..."

incident-bot: Escalation: on-call rotation -> paged tara as secondary.

alex (oncall): Tara, fyi. We're mitigating. Main blocker: cloud GPU quota. Next step: request emergency quota bump OR spin up in us-east1.

tariq (runtime): Starting cross-region spin-up to us-east1 as fallback. Provision command:
```
redwoodctl pool create inference-east --region us-east1 --nodes 6 --gpu-type a100
```
Provisioning started. ETA ~8-12m.

maria (sre): In the meantime, increased KV prefix caching to reduce token generation for repeated prompts, hoping to reduce token load.

sam (eng): I've deployed a temporary lightweight quantized model variant (gptq-8bit) to handle low-priority workloads to reduce GPU consumption.

alex (oncall): Good. Monitor queue and p99. Hold page updates every 10 minutes.

-- 10 minutes later --

tariq (runtime): inference-east pool is healthy and registered. Route reconfiguration:
```
redwoodctl routing set policy --match region:us-east1 --pool inference-east --selector low-priority
```
Traffic shifted. Queue decreased from 1200 -> 220 in 6 minutes.

maria (sre): p99 latency improved from 10s -> 600ms for enterprise routes. Free-tier still throttled.

kelly (support): Sent update to affected customers. Response: cust-omega needs SLA note; escalated to account team.

alex (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will continue to monitor for 1h before declaring resolved.

-- Post-incident notes / actions --

alex (oncall): Summary: Root cause: cloud GPU quota exhausted in us-west1 combined with autoscaler retries hitting cloud API rate limits. Mitigation: throttled free-tier, spun up fallback pool in us-east1, deployed quantized model to reduce consumption. Time to mitigation ~32 minutes.

action-items:
- tariq: submit emergency quota request and follow up with cloud rep. (owner: tariq, due: 2025-11-30)
- sam: bake quantized model into canary pipeline and verify perf/quality tradeoffs. (owner: sam, due: 2025-12-07)
- maria: add autoscaler retry/backoff telemetry and alert for quota-exhaustion specifically. (owner: maria, due: 2025-11-25)
- eng-platform: run chaos test for GPU pool quota exhaustion and autoscaler fallback (owner: eng-platform, due: 2025-12-15)

alex (oncall): Schedule postmortem doc and link to incident timeline. I'll own the timeline doc and coordinate a blameless review tomorrow 10am PT.

incident-bot: Incident state changed -> MITIGATED by alex at 1752507320

maria (sre): Adding logs and snippets to the postmortem.

kelly (support): Crafting customer-facing post-incident summary.

alex (oncall): Thanks team. Closing active paging. If anything regresses, re-open channel.
